_comment: Blueprint 8.3 — seccomp hardening for the rb-ai-team devcontainer. Strategy: default-allow with an explicit deny of high-risk syscalls that normal Node/npm/git/tsx workloads never use but are classic kernel-manipulation / container-escape primitives. This is guaranteed not to EPERM the toolchain (unlike a strict allowlist) and coexists with the docker-in-docker feature. NEXT STEP: once the container can be built in CI, tighten to a Docker-default-style allowlist (defaultAction SCMP_ACT_ERRNO) and iterate on any EPERM. eBPF is intentionally blocked here; note that eBPF-based enforcement is Linux/CI-only and unavailable under WSL2 — seccomp is the portable hardening step.

syscalls.comment: Kernel module loading, kexec, kernel keyring, reboot, swap, eBPF, process tracing/memory access, and legacy sysctl/nfs control — none used by Node/npm/git; all are container-escape or kernel-tampering primitives.
